subject: MAP Close Plan: signal labelling, smoke-test sprint, and rollback windows
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alisa Kumar <alisa@medinova.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Oct 2025 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: MAP Close Plan: signal labelling, smoke-test sprint, and rollback windows

Hi Alisa (and team),

Following our kickoff, I put a very short, operational-first MAP extract together so we can align on exactly what 'success' looks for the evaluation and what evidence you need to sign off. Key asks below — I kept this intentionally minimal so we can lock it in before the demo sprint. Attached: MAP-v1.xlsx and a lightweight smoke-tests-runbook.md.

Summary (asks for this week):
- Confirm three primary success signals (functional, latency, and data-safety) by EOD Wed.
- Agree on the smoke-test sprint window: Oct 20–24 (we'll run daily smoke runs and produce pass/fail artifacts).
- Confirm rollback windows and severity-based escalation lanes (we propose 4-hour mitigation SLA for sev-1 during smoke).

Proposed Success Signal labels (please confirm or rename):
1) Functional-pass-rate >= 92% on chosen prompt set (see sheet "smoke-set") — pass/fail per run.
2) Median inference latency <= 220ms (p95 <= 400ms) for 2k token median workload.
3) Data isolation & auditability: KV traceability for 100% of sampled requests + access logs captured for 72hrs.

Exit gates (hard):
- No sev-1 regressions open at time of handoff.
- All required test cases in smoke run marked PASS and artifacts uploaded to shared Drive.
- Compliance checklist (SOC/trace evidence) validated by your security lead.

Acceptance tests (deliverables):
- Daily smoke report (CSV + short notes).
- Load-sampled traces (redacted) demonstrating KV caching behavior.
- A runbook for cutover/rollback with concrete steps and owner.

If that reads OK I can escalate the MAP document to production owners and we will create the HubSpot milestone. If you want different thresholds for the functional-pass-rate or latency, tell us where to tune — those are adjustable.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-v1.xlsx (sheet: smoke-set, owners), smoke-tests-runbook.md

From: Alisa Kumar <alisa@medinova.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Oct 2025 09:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP Close Plan: signal labelling, smoke-test sprint, and rollback windows

Thanks, Laura — this is close to what we need. A few quick clarifications from our side:

1) Functional-pass-rate: can you split the smoke-set into core-critical (20 prompts) vs secondary (30 prompts) and give separate pass rates? For signoff we want core-critical >= 95%.
2) Latency: good baseline. Can we add a soft target for CPU-hosted fallbacks (p95 <= 800ms)? We expect a fallback during one window.
3) Data isolation: Procurement will need a statement on data retention (how long logs are retained in the private deployment). 72hrs is fine for smoke but we need a formal policy for the contract.

Procurement note: I've looped procurement (procurement@medinova.com) and VP Eng (jmorgan@medinova.com) for the contract window; they asked whether we can get DocuSign by Oct 24.

Can we schedule a 30m alignment tomorrow to finalize thresholds?

— Alisa
Director, Product (MediNova)

Date: Wed, 08 Oct 2025 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP Close Plan: signal labelling, smoke-test sprint, and rollback windows

Thanks Alisa — good call splitting core vs secondary. Updated plan below (I also attached SLA-exceptions.docx per procurement request). Proposed changes: 

- Functional-pass-rate: core-critical (20 prompts) >= 95% required; secondary (30 prompts) >= 88% advisory.
- Latency: primary target unchanged (median <= 220ms, p95 <= 400ms). Soft fallback target: CPU-hosted p95 <= 800ms — will be an advisory metric for this eval (we'll show evidence).
- Data retention: smoke: 72hrs. Contractually: configurable retention windows (72hrs–90 days) — we'll provide the policy statement in the contract addendum.

Rollbacks / Escalation lanes (operational):
- Sev-1 during smoke run: immediate rollback to previous model variant + notify both parties; 4-hour remediation window to either fix or open an approved exception.
- Sev-2: patch in next day, tracked via shared Jira (link in Drive).

Deliverables / Evidence (what you'll see each day):
- smoke-report-YYYYMMDD.csv (per-run pass/fail per test)
- traced-sample-YYYYMMDD.json (redacted traces showing cache hits)
- operations-summary-YYYYMMDD.md (short narrative of issues + owner)

Next steps:
1) Quick sync tomorrow, Oct 9 at 10:00 AM PT — proposed 30m.
2) We freeze the MAP thresholds and we prepare the DocuSign package (target: Oct 24 completion).

If that works I'll create a HubSpot milestone and lock the smoke-run schedule.

Best,
Laura

Attachments: SLA-exceptions.docx
